clusters.title: MI35x runner nodes' GPUs were already ~98% full before jobs started — nightly-test-amd, pr-test-amd, Miles · ❌ no fix

details.label: Status
details.text: first seen Nov 10 02:34 UTC on `mia1-p02-g14`. Since then, 18 jobs failed on 6 nodes: `g12`, `g16`, `g25`, `g26`, `g27` and `g14`. 13 of them were in one run, [Nightly, Nov 10 16:08, rocm10](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42851533488). `g16` was still full at 23:16. Each job had passed this check in its previous 14–15 runs. Other nodes passed the check in the same minutes.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` no change is blamed. Processes outside the runner pod held about 300 GB per GPU before the job started any container:
8 KFD PIDs with consecutive numbers, invisible to `fuser`.
The cleanup's SIGKILLs had no effect.
The GPUs were busy: CU occupancy and memory activity changed between checks.
On `g26` the GPUs filled up after the check passed, and the HiCache server then aborted with `memory capacity is unbalanced`.
**Disconfirming**: the pod cannot see who owns the PIDs. It could be another tenant's live workload, or the server of an earlier job that outlived its pod.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found. [#49387](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49387) moves `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x` to the Spur runners. It is related, but it does not fix these nodes.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: runner owners run `kubectl get pods -A -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=mia1-p02-g16` (and the same for the other nodes), then check the host PIDs. Take the nodes out of service until they are clean, and re-run the failed jobs.

clusters.title: Two new tests from the MiniMax-H3-Image PR fail on ROCm

details.label: Status
details.text: first seen Nov 10 19:50 UTC in [PR Test, Nov 10 19:02, rocm724](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42881201765). This is the first scheduled run that contains [#49552](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49552). Neither test has run on rocm10 or rocm720 yet.

Layerwise offload: `[HIGH]` [#49552](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49552) ([`170804b4`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/170804b40a403881256b600ffb337e23f37b4e30)) creates `Event(external=True)` during breakable-graph capture (`layerwise_offload.py:2175`, `[FACT]`). The ROCm build of PyTorch rejects external events, so the capture falls back to eager and the new test fails.
Online FP8: `[HIGH]` the same PR added `test_online_fp8_layerwise_load.py`. It calls `.view(torch.uint8)` on the 0-dim per-tensor FP8 scale.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: only one run and one ROCm version so far. The design may be CUDA-only, in which case a ROCm skip is the fix.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found. I searched `layerwise offload`, `External events` and `test_online_fp8_layerwise_load`.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: the PR author decides between a ROCm path and a ROCm skip for both tests.

details.label: DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 on MI300 (rocm724, last seen Oct 21)
details.text: the server aborted with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES … Free mem: 0 MB` under the GSM8K burst. `[MEDIUM]` No change is blamed: `--mem-fraction-static 0.90` leaves almost no headroom for allocations outside the torch pool. details.text: `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` in aiter `paged_attention_ll4mi_QKV_mfma16_kernel` during LoRA and fully-async decode. Two 1800 s timeouts followed, and the step ran out of its 180 min, so 20 tests never ran. `[MEDIUM]` A faulty host behind pod subnet `10.42.22.0/24`: both MI35x occurrences (Oct 31, Nov 9) ran there.

details.text: on Oct 31 the same fault also hit a Miles MI300 LoRA test, which ran on a different host.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: map `10.42.22.x` to its node and check its GPU health. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, try a lower `--mem-fraction-static` on a branch.
